newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds firm, EU seals deal on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds firm, EU seals deal on stability pact.

text.p: Irish bonds firmed in thin late trade on Friday on news that EU heads of state had reached a deal on a stability pact at their summit meeting in Dublin, dealers said.
The European Union reached a deal on a pact to enforce a budget discipline after its planned monetary union is launched in 1999, diplomats and officials said.
"All the 15 countries have agreed," Swedish finance minister Erik Asbrink told reporters.
Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn told a news conference that officials had agreed the entire document.

He was referring to a package of measures, including the stability pact, to penalise states which run big fiscal deficits under monetary union, meant to lay down a detailed framework for how economic and monetary union (EMU) would work.
By 1610 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had firmed 45 pence to 100.95 to yield 6.26 percent having been as low as 100.35 earlier in the day.
The eight percent bond due 2006 was up 30 pence at 107.60 to yield 6.80 percent having been at 106.95 earlier.

Dealers said the market had also been helped by steady T-notes after the U.S. University of Michigan preliminary December consumer confidence survey fell to 98.9 against 99.2 in November. --Damien Lynch, Dublin newsroom 353-1-660-3377.
